x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the TRIPS waiver was proposed by India and South Africa.

st.3: The Department of Border Management, created in 2004, is part of the Ministry of Defence.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Department of Border Management is under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

st.2: Part XIVA (Tribunals) was added by the 74th Amendment, 1992.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Part XIVA (Tribunals) was added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976; the 74th Amendment added Part IXA (Municipalities).

st.1: Ram Jawaya Kapur (1955) held that the Constitution adopts a rigid separation of powers.
st.2: In Raj Narain (1975), the Supreme Court held that the legislature may finally decide an election dispute itself.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Ram Jawaya Kapur held there is no rigid separation of powers. Statement 2 is wrong: Raj Narain struck down the 39th Amendment clause that took the PM's election dispute out of the courts.

st.2: Canning nominated the Raja of Benaras, the Maharaja of Patiala and Sir Syed Ahmad Khan to the legislative council.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Canning nominated the Raja of Benaras, the Maharaja of Patiala and Sir Dinkar Rao.

st.2: The Constitution of India came into force on 26 January 1950, the day the members signed it.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: members signed the Constitution on 24 January 1950; it came into force on 26 January 1950.
Both statements are correct: the Mountbatten Plan was announced on 3 June 1947 and accepted by both the Congress and the Muslim League.

st.3: Constitution Day (26 November) marks the day the Constitution came into force.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: 26 November marks the adoption of the Constitution (1949); it came into force on 26 January 1950.

st.3: Freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse was borrowed from Canada.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse was borrowed from Australia.

st.2: The original Constitution already contained the Ninth Schedule.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the original Constitution had 8 Schedules; the Ninth was added by the 1st Amendment, 1951.

st.1: Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission, a statutory body set up by Parliament.
st.3: Article 300A makes the right to property a Fundamental Right.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Finance Commission under Article 280 is a constitutional body. Statement 3 is wrong: Article 300A makes property a constitutional (legal) right, not a Fundamental Right.
Both statements are correct: Anuradha Bhasin required internet shutdowns to be proportionate, temporary and published, and recognised internet speech and trade under Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(g).

st.1: During a National Emergency, the President can suspend the right to move courts for enforcement of Articles 20 and 21.
st.2: This protection of Articles 20 and 21 was added by the 42nd Amendment.
st.3: Under Article 33, State legislatures may restrict the Fundamental Rights of the police.

x: Statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended. Statement 2 is wrong: the protection was added by the 44th Amendment. Statement 3 is wrong: under Article 33 only Parliament can restrict these rights.

st.1: S.R. Bommai held that a proclamation under Article 356 is immune from judicial review.
st.3: Rameshwar Prasad (2006) declared the dissolution of the Jharkhand Assembly void.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Bommai (nine judges) held an Article 356 proclamation judicially reviewable. Statement 3 is wrong: Rameshwar Prasad concerned the dissolution of the Bihar Assembly.

st.1: Under Article 331 the President could nominate two Anglo-Indians to the Rajya Sabha; the 104th Amendment did not extend this.
st.3: The 104th Amendment also provided 10% reservation for the economically weaker sections.
st.4: Reservation of Lok Sabha seats for SCs and STs under Article 330 was made permanent by the original Constitution.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Article 331 nominations were to the Lok Sabha. Statement 3 is wrong: EWS reservation came by the 103rd Amendment. Statement 4 is wrong: it was initially for ten years and has been extended since.

st.2: On prorogation, pending Bills lapse.
st.3: After prorogation, the Speaker can summon the House.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: prorogation does not make pending Bills lapse. Statement 3 is wrong: only the President can summon the House after prorogation.

st.1: Zero Hour is provided for in the Rules of Procedure of the Lok Sabha.
st.3: Ministers are bound to reply to the matters raised in Zero Hour.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Zero Hour is not mentioned in the Rules of Procedure. Statement 3 is wrong: ministers are not bound to reply in Zero Hour.

st.2: It can be moved only in the Lok Sabha.
st.3: It is referred to the Ethics Committee.
st.4: If adopted, it forces the Government to resign.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: it can be moved in either House. Statement 3 is wrong: it is referred to the Committee of Privileges. Statement 4 is wrong: it censures the Minister and does not force the Government out.

st.2: The Economic Stabilisation Fund was proposed in the Interim Budget 2019-20.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Economic Stabilisation Fund (Rs 1 lakh crore) was proposed in the Union Budget 2026-27.

st.3: The Committee of Privileges of the Lok Sabha is a joint committee of both Houses.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: each House has its own Committee of Privileges; the Lok Sabha one has 15 members.

st.1: The Cabinet Secretary is a member of the Union Council of Ministers.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Cabinet Secretary is a civil servant, the head of the Cabinet Secretariat, not a minister.

st.2: His remuneration is fixed by Parliament by law.
st.4: He performs duties of a legal character referred or assigned to him by the Chief Justice of India.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the AG's remuneration is determined by the President. Statement 4 is wrong: he performs legal duties referred or assigned by the President.

st.1: The President may direct the Governor to return even a Money Bill for reconsideration.
st.2: The State Legislature is under no obligation to reconsider a returned Bill.
st.3: The President is bound to assent to the Bill if it is passed again.

x: Statement 4 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: a Money Bill cannot be returned for reconsideration. Statement 2 is wrong: a returned Bill must be reconsidered within six months. Statement 3 is wrong: the President is not bound to assent even if it is passed again.

st.2: The State has a constitutional counterpart of the Vice-President.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: there is no office in the State corresponding to the Vice-President.

st.1: He is removed by an order of the Governor after an address by both Houses of Parliament passed with a special majority.
st.3: Justice Soumitra Sen of the Calcutta High Court resigned in 2011 after the Lok Sabha voted for his removal.
st.4: The State Legislature may remove a High Court judge by a resolution passed by a two-thirds majority.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the removal order is issued by the President, not the Governor. Statement 3 is wrong: Soumitra Sen resigned after the Rajya Sabha voted for his removal, before the Lok Sabha took it up. Statement 4 is wrong: the State Legislature has no role in removing a High Court judge.

st.2: Upendra Baxi argued that courts should replace democratic institutions that fail to act.
st.3: The PIL rethink debate of May 2026 sought to abolish access to justice through PIL.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Baxi said courts should fill a vacuum, not replace democratic institutions. Statement 3 is wrong: the May 2026 debate was about curbing PIL misuse, not abolishing access to justice.

st.2: The President is the Head of the Government, not merely the Head of the State.

x: Both statements are correct: the President holds Rank 1 in the Order of Precedence and is the Head of the State, while the Prime Minister heads the Government.

st.1: It is a quasi-judicial body constituted by Parliament under Article 280 every fifth year or earlier.
st.3: Cesses and surcharges form part of the divisible pool shared with the States.
st.4: The southern States' 'Chalo Delhi' protest of 2024 mainly opposed the tax-effort criterion in devolution.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Finance Commission is constituted by the President. Statement 3 is wrong: cesses and surcharges stay outside the divisible pool, so effective devolution is only about 31-32%. Statement 4 is wrong: 'Chalo Delhi' opposed the population-based criteria.

st.2: AP's share under the 16th Finance Commission is higher than under the 14th.
st.3: Special Category Status for AP was written into the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: AP's 16th FC share (4.217%) is lower than its 14th FC share (4.305%). Statement 3 is wrong: Special Category Status was only an assurance in Parliament, not part of the Act.

st.3: It can inquire into any matter regardless of when the alleged violation took place.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: the selection committee includes the Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman and the Home Minister, the term is three years or 70 years of age, and the NHRC cannot inquire into a matter more than one year after the alleged violation.

st.1: The NHRC was constituted on 12 October 1993 with Justice J.S. Verma as its first Chairperson.
st.3: The Protection of Human Rights Act received assent in January 1994, before the NHRC was constituted.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: the Ordinance came on 28 September 1993 and the Act in January 1994, after the NHRC was set up. Statement 1 is wrong: the first Chairperson was Justice Ranganath Misra.

st.4: The Governor should belong to the State in which he is appointed.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: Sarkaria wanted the Governor to be from outside the State and detached from its local politics.

st.3: It was appointed after the Rajamannar Committee but before the Sarkaria Commission.
st.4: It was to review Centre-State arrangements in the light of changes since the States Reorganisation Commission.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the order is Rajamannar (1969), Sarkaria (1983), Punchhi (2007). Statement 4 is wrong: it was to review changes since the Sarkaria Commission.

st.2: Cesses and surcharges were to be left unlimited.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Punchhi Commission wanted cesses and surcharges reviewed and kept in check so that the States' share is not eroded.

st.4: The NETA app, which lets voters rate their representatives, was developed by the ECI.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the NETA app is a private initiative, not an ECI app.

st.3: Article 83, which may need amending for simultaneous elections, deals with the duration of State Legislatures.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Article 83 deals with the duration of the Houses of Parliament; Article 172 covers State Legislatures.

st.2: Andhra Pradesh was the first State to introduce Panchayati Raj.
st.3: Kasu Brahmananda Reddy was the Minister for Local Bodies in Damodaram Sanjivayya's cabinet.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Rajasthan was first; Andhra Pradesh was second, on 1 November 1959. Statement 3 is wrong: Kasu Brahmananda Reddy was Minister for Local Bodies in N. Sanjiva Reddy's cabinet.

st.3: PM-WANI public Wi-Fi hotspots are implemented by MeitY.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: PM-WANI is run by the Department of Telecommunications.

st.2: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh lends directly to individual poor women without intermediaries.
st.3: DAY-NRLM, implemented by the Ministry of Women and Child Development, uses Poshan Sakhis among its community resource persons.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: RMK lends through intermediary organisations such as NGOs and MFIs. Statement 3 is wrong: DAY-NRLM is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development.

st.4: DPRs have been completed for all 30 links.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: PFRs are done for all 30 links, but DPRs only for 14.

st.3: In NMP 1.0, roads yielded the largest monetisation proceeds.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: roads were the largest sector in the plan, but coal gave the largest proceeds in NMP 1.0.

st.2: SC households had higher latrine access than the all-India average.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: SC households lagged the all-India average in latrine access.

st.3: Assam's Small Family Norms bar parents of more than two children from contesting Lok Sabha elections.
st.4: Uttar Pradesh's draft Population Bill was released by the Union Health Ministry.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Assam's norm bars them from State government jobs (from 2021), not Lok Sabha elections. Statement 4 is wrong: UP's draft Bill (July 2021) was released by the UP State Law Commission.

st.2: By July 2025 the entire central share had been claimed.
st.3: The mission has never been extended beyond its original deadline.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: about 99% (Rs 47,459 crore), not all, of the central share had been claimed. Statement 3 is wrong: the mission has been extended to 2025-26.

st.1: Education takes a larger share of spending than the all-States average.
st.3: Health has the largest outlay of all departments.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: education's 11.7% is below the all-States average of 14.5%. Statement 3 is wrong: School Education has the largest outlay; Health (Rs 19,306 crore) is fourth.

st.2: Placement is optional, with no minimum placement required in State skill schemes.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: a minimum placement of 70% is required in all State skill schemes.

st.1: It covers only classes I to V in government and aided schools.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: PM POSHAN covers Bal Vatika and classes I to VIII.

st.3: GVA at basic prices has been dropped as the headline sectoral measure in the 2022-23 series.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: GVA at basic prices has been the headline sectoral measure since the 2011-12 series and remains so in the 2022-23 series.

st.1: Supply of resources is its only function.
st.2: Recycling is one of its functions.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the environment also assimilates waste, sustains life and gives aesthetic services. Statement 2 is wrong: the four functions are supply of resources, assimilation of waste, sustaining life and aesthetic services; recycling is not one of them.

st.3: The Dandekar-Rath study (1971) used 2,400 kcal for rural and 2,100 kcal for urban areas.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Dandekar-Rath used 2,250 kcal for both; 2,400 / 2,100 kcal is the Alagh (1979) norm.

st.2: The inequality reports released at Davos are published by the World Economic Forum.
st.3: The Global Wealth Report and Databook is associated with the World Bank.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Davos inequality reports are published by Oxfam. Statement 3 is wrong: the Global Wealth Report is associated with Credit Suisse (now UBS).

st.2: It executed the plans through its own field offices in the States.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Planning Commission only formulated and appraised plans; execution was by the ministries and State governments.

st.2: After the Gulf War of August 1990, oil prices doubled and Gulf remittances rose.
st.3: The New Economic Policy was launched by the Chandra Shekhar government.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: after the Gulf War oil prices rose while Gulf remittances fell. Statement 3 is wrong: the Chandra Shekhar government fell before the NEP, which came under P.V. Narasimha Rao in July 1991.

st.2: The 2018 Standing Orders Rules allowed fixed-term employment only in the apparel sector.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 2018 rules extended fixed-term employment to all sectors; only the 2016 rules were limited to apparel.

st.1: It includes cesses and surcharges.

x: Both statements are correct: the divisible pool excludes cesses and surcharges and was about 81% of gross tax revenue in 2025-26.

st.2: The 16th FC recommended an annual disclosure of net tax proceeds certified by the Union Finance Ministry.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 16th FC recommended an annual disclosure of net tax proceeds certified by the CAG.
Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: the MUDRA cap was ₹10 lakh at launch, 'Tarun Plus' (₹10-20 lakh) is for good Tarun borrowers, and guarantees come through CGTMSE.

st.3: Reducing the financial security of households by shifting them away from informal savings is one of its outcomes.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: financial inclusion aims to increase, not reduce, households' financial security.

st.1: It is compiled and published by the NPCI.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the DPI is compiled and published by the RBI, semi-annually.

st.1: The RBI's Central Office was first set up in Bombay and later moved to Calcutta.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Central Office began in Calcutta and was moved to Bombay in 1937.

st.2: The SLR is governed by Section 42 of the RBI Act, 1934.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the SLR is governed by Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949; Section 42 of the RBI Act covers the CRR.

st.2: The scheme is named after Indira Gandhi.
st.3: State and central health schemes together cover every household in AP (2026).

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Aarogyasri was named after Rajiv Gandhi. Statement 3 is wrong: the schemes together cover about 70% of AP households, not all.

st.2: It manages the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF), which is funded by State government contributions.
st.3: Its SHG-Bank Linkage Programme, piloted in 1992, is implemented only through RRBs and cooperative banks.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: RIDF is funded by banks' priority-sector lending shortfalls. Statement 3 is wrong: SHG-BLP runs through commercial banks as well as RRBs and cooperative banks.

st.2: Headline inflation is more stable than core inflation.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: headline inflation includes food and fuel and is more volatile than core inflation.
Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: the general government debt target is 60% of GDP, split 40% Centre and 20% States, following the N.K. Singh Committee (2017).

st.3: Management of money supply and liquidity
st.4: Regulation of inter-state trade

x: 1 and 2 are objectives of fiscal policy. 3 is not: money supply and liquidity are managed by monetary policy (RBI). 4 is not: regulating inter-state trade is a legislative and regulatory matter, not a fiscal-policy objective.

st.1: The FRBM Rules, 2004 required the fiscal deficit to be cut by 0.3% of GDP every year, with no annual target for the revenue deficit.
st.3: The tax-GDP ratio is a legally binding target under the Act.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Rules also required the revenue deficit to fall by 0.5% of GDP each year. Statement 3 is wrong: the tax-GDP ratio is not a binding target under the FRBM Act.

st.2: Budget 2015-16 abolished service tax and replaced it with GST.
st.3: From 2012-13 it applied to all services except those in a positive list.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Budget 2015-16 raised the rate from 12% to 14%; GST replaced service tax only in 2017. Statement 3 is wrong: from 2012-13 it applied to all services except those in a negative list.

st.1: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, India had a merchandise trade surplus in FY25.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: India had a merchandise trade deficit of about $283.5 bn in FY25; the surplus was in services.

st.2: In 2018-19, China was India's largest trading partner.
st.3: Russia was India's largest export market among BRICS members in FY 2025-26.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the USA was India's largest trading partner from 2018-19 to 2024-25. Statement 3 is wrong: the UAE was India's largest BRICS export market in FY 2025-26.

st.4: Marine products have been the largest agricultural export in recent years.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: marine products led only in the late 1990s; in recent years cereals (rice) are the largest agricultural export.

st.1: The World Bank acts as lender of last resort to a country whose reserves cannot cover its BoP deficit.
st.3: Concessional lending to low-income countries is the IMF's core function.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: it is the IMF, not the World Bank, that lends to countries in BoP crisis. Statement 3 is wrong: the IMF's core function is BoP support; concessional development lending is the World Bank's (IDA) role.

st.3: After paddy, maize was the largest foodgrain group by area in 2024-25.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: pulses (11.66 lakh ha) were second after paddy in 2024-25; maize had only 3.20 lakh ha.

st.2: It is associated with Verghese Kurien.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Verghese Kurien is linked with the White Revolution; the Yellow Revolution is associated with Sam Pitroda.

st.2: It provides 100% MSP procurement of moong and chana.
st.3: The PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana covers 100 high-productivity districts.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the pulses mission promises 100% MSP procurement of tur, urad and masoor. Statement 3 is wrong: PMDDKY covers 100 low-productivity districts.

st.2: Recorded bargadars got no heritable rights.
st.3: Under it, the landowner was entitled to 75% of the produce.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: recorded bargadars got heritable rights. Statement 3 is wrong: the bargadar, not the landowner, got 75% of the produce (when supplying inputs).

st.1: Under 'One State, One RRB', Andhra Pradesh's four RRBs were merged into two banks from 1 May 2025.
st.2: The sponsor bank of Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank is the State Bank of India.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the four RRBs became a single Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank. Statement 2 is wrong: its sponsor bank is Union Bank of India.

st.2: It took over RBI's ACD and RPCC and the whole of the Industrial Finance Corporation of India.
st.3: It began with a capital of Rs 100 crore, has its headquarters at Mumbai and has been fully owned by the RBI since 2019.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: NABARD took over the ACD, RPCC and the Agricultural Refinance and Development Corporation, not IFCI. Statement 3 is wrong: NABARD has been fully owned by the Government of India since 2019, after the RBI divested its stake.

st.2: In 2024-25, every e-NAM market of AP took part in inter-mandi trade.
st.3: Produce stored in WDRA-regulated warehouses cannot be sold on e-NAM.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: only 11 of AP's 33 e-NAM mandis took part in inter-mandi trade. Statement 3 is wrong: warehouse produce can be sold on e-NAM using e-NWRs.

st.2: The Price Stabilisation Fund of 2015 creates buffers of rice and wheat.
st.3: In November 2020, Punjab became the first State to fix floor prices for vegetables.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the PSF builds buffers of onion, potato and pulses. Statement 3 is wrong: it was Kerala that fixed floor prices for 16 vegetables in November 2020.

st.2: Anna Darpan is meant to modernise the supply chain of NAFED.
st.4: Export of foodgrains is a stated objective of food management in India.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Anna Darpan modernises FCI's supply chain. Statement 4 is wrong: export of foodgrains is not an objective of food management.

st.1: The cotton mills were foreign-dominated.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the early cotton mills were mostly Indian-owned, while the jute mills were foreign-dominated.

st.1: Manufacturing accounts for the largest share of these units.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: services (48%) are the largest share; manufacturing has only about 24%.

st.2: It is implemented by SIDBI.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: PMEGP is implemented by KVIC at the national level.

st.1: Industrial sickness raises the revenue of the exchequer as idle assets are sold.
st.3: Sickness has been concentrated in software services rather than in textiles, jute and sugar.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: sickness locks up capital and reduces revenue. Statement 3 is wrong: sickness has been concentrated in textiles, jute, sugar and engineering, not software.

st.1: It earns foreign exchange but creates no formal jobs.
st.3: On its own, it delivers broad-based development across India.

x: Statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: IT/ITES earns foreign exchange and does create formal jobs. Statement 3 is wrong: its benefits are concentrated in a few cities and skills, so it cannot deliver broad-based development on its own.

st.2: In 2024-25, Andhra Pradesh's capital outlay exceeded its revenue spending.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: AP's revenue spending (₹2,24,343 crore) dwarfed its capital outlay (₹24,072 crore) in 2024-25.

st.2: The 1,372 m diaphragm wall, rebuilt from January 2025, was completed at no extra cost.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the rebuilt diaphragm wall (completed in 440 days) cost about ₹1,000 crore extra.

st.1: The State faces a loss of up to Rs 38,000 crore because the 16th Finance Commission raised revenue deficit grants.

x: Both statements are correct: the loss of up to Rs 38,000 crore is because the 16th FC dropped revenue deficit grants, and the revenue deficit is projected at Rs 48,000 crore in 2025-26.

st.2: Paddy output was 127.15 lakh tonnes, with rabi output higher than kharif output.
st.3: Food-grain production of 161.86 lakh tonnes came from a smaller area than in 2023-24.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: kharif paddy output (78.79 lakh t) was higher than rabi (48.36 lakh t). Statement 3 is wrong: production was 161.86 lakh t, but the food-grain area rose from 33.24 to 37.51 lakh ha.

st.2: Its markets are completely independent of foreign demand.
st.3: It supports over five lakh families, all of them in the Rayalaseema districts.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: AP aquaculture depends heavily on export markets. Statement 3 is wrong: it supports over five lakh families, mainly in the coastal Godavari-Krishna belt, not Rayalaseema.

st.3: The PRASHAD scheme is run by the Union Ministry of Culture.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: PRASHAD is run by the Union Ministry of Tourism.

st.2: Angel tax remains in force for all start-ups.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: angel tax was abolished for all classes of investors in the Union Budget 2024-25.

st.2: Andhra Pradesh topped the N-LRSI in 2021.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Madhya Pradesh topped the N-LRSI; AP rose from 10th (2020) to 6th (2021).

st.1: IREDA, which finances renewable energy and energy-efficiency projects, works under the Ministry of Power.

x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: IREDA works under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.

st.3: Stars below the Chandrasekhar limit end as black holes.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: stars below the Chandrasekhar limit end as white dwarfs; heavier remnants collapse to neutron stars or black holes.

st.2: The tilt of the Earth's axis, not the changing Earth–Sun distance, is the main cause of seasons.

x: Both statements are correct: aphelion falls in early July, and seasons are caused mainly by the tilt of the Earth's axis rather than by distance.

st.2: Srinagar gets the overhead noon Sun on the summer solstice.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Srinagar lies north of the Tropic of Cancer and never gets the overhead noon Sun.

st.2: The formation of clay from feldspar is an example of hydrolysis.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: oxidation rusts iron minerals, feldspar turns to clay by hydrolysis, and roots and burrowing animals cause biological weathering.

st.2: North Macedonia has a short coastline on the Adriatic.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: North Macedonia is landlocked and has no Adriatic coastline.

st.2: The Hagari valley records the lowest rainfall in the State.
st.3: The Sileru and Sabari valleys record the lowest rainfall in the State.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: the Hagari valley is the driest part of AP. Statement 3 is wrong: the Sileru and Sabari valleys record the highest rainfall in the State.

st.2: UV-B (280–315 nm) is mostly absorbed by the ozone layer, though part of it reaches the ground.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: UV-A mostly reaches the surface, UV-B is mostly absorbed with some reaching the ground, and UV-C is the shortest and most harmful.

st.3: The Norwegian Current is a cold current of the North Atlantic.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Norwegian Current is a warm current, an extension of the North Atlantic Drift.

st.2: Saramati is the highest peak of Manipur.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Saramati (3,826 m) is the highest peak of Nagaland, in the Naga Hills.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Vande Mataram was written in Sanskrit (Sanskritised Bengali), not Hindi.

st.1: Patient Advisory Councils are recommended under UNICEF's Global Patient Safety Action Plan.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Global Patient Safety Action Plan is WHO's, not UNICEF's.

st.2: Bunker Roy's wife is activist Medha Patkar.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Bunker Roy's wife is activist Aruna Roy (MKSS, RTI movement).

st.2: Its motto is "Sham No Varunah".
st.3: The Chief of Defence Staff is the Supreme Commander of the IAF.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the IAF motto is 'Nabhah Sparsham Deeptam'; 'Sham No Varunah' is the Navy's. Statement 3 is wrong: the President is the Supreme Commander of the armed forces.

st.1: R.M. Nachammai became the first woman Chief Superintendent of the Kaiga nuclear power station in Andhra Pradesh.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Kaiga nuclear power station is in Karnataka.

st.3: Bobby Mukkamala, with roots in Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh, became the first person of Indian heritage to head the World Medical Association.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Bobby Mukkamala heads the American Medical Association, not the World Medical Association.

st.3: The DGCA is responsible for aviation security.
st.4: ICAO is headquartered at Geneva.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: aviation security is the job of the BCAS; the DGCA is the safety regulator. Statement 4 is wrong: ICAO is headquartered at Montreal.

st.3: Under Section 3A (added in 2003), a repeat offence attracts only a fine.
st.4: It makes the singing of Vande Mataram compulsory.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: a repeat offence under Section 3A carries a minimum of one year's imprisonment. Statement 4 is wrong: the Act does not make singing compulsory.

st.3: Leila Seth, the first woman Chief Justice of a High Court, headed the Delhi High Court.
st.4: Justice Yashwant Varma addressed his resignation to the Chief Justice of India.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Leila Seth was Chief Justice of the Himachal Pradesh High Court. Statement 4 is wrong: a judge's resignation is addressed to the President.

st.2: The 2018 five-judge verdict was 4:1, with the lone dissent by Justice R.F. Nariman.
st.3: The temple lies in the Periyar Tiger Reserve and is run by the Cochin Devaswom Board.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the lone dissent in the 2018 verdict was by Justice Indu Malhotra. Statement 3 is wrong: Sabarimala is run by the Travancore Devaswom Board.

st.2: The 84th Amendment allowed Lok Sabha seats to be redistributed among States on the 2001 Census.
st.4: Delimitation orders can be challenged before the High Court.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 84th Amendment kept the inter-State allocation frozen on the 1971 Census till the first Census after 2026. Statement 4 is wrong: delimitation orders cannot be questioned in any court.

st.2: In Subramanian Swamy v Union of India (2016) the Supreme Court struck it down as violating Article 19(1)(a).

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Subramanian Swamy (2016) upheld criminal defamation, treating reputation as part of Article 21.

st.1: Assam, Kerala and Tamil Nadu polled on 9 April 2026.
st.2: Tamil Nadu was the only State to poll in two phases.
st.3: Votes in Assam, Kerala and Puducherry were counted before polling ended in West Bengal.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Assam, Kerala and Puducherry polled on 9 April; Tamil Nadu polled on 23 April. Statement 2 is wrong: West Bengal was the only two-phase State. Statement 3 is wrong: all votes were counted together on 4 May 2026.

st.2: The Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Act, 2026 replaced a GST Ordinance.
st.4: A Registered Unrecognised Political Party gets a reserved symbol.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 2026 taxation law did not replace any GST Ordinance. Statement 4 is wrong: a RUPP gets only a free (common) symbol on conditions; reserved symbols are for recognised parties.

st.3: The 131st Amendment Bill was passed by the Lok Sabha but defeated in the Rajya Sabha.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 131st Amendment Bill was defeated in the Lok Sabha itself, on 17 April 2026.

st.1: The National Bamboo Mission is run by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the National Bamboo Mission is run by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.

st.3: The World Food India 2026 Southern Regional Conference, its first regional edition, was held at Chennai.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the first regional edition was held at Visakhapatnam.

st.3: Namo Drone Didi is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for women SHGs.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Namo Drone Didi is a Central Sector scheme, fully funded by the Centre.

st.1: India is a full member of the International Energy Agency, whose storage norm is 90 days.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: India is only an association country of the IEA, not a full member.

st.3: The ₹1 lakh crore Urban Challenge Fund bears the full cost of the projects it supports.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the fund covers up to 25% of a bankable project's cost (Centre 25%, States 25%, market 50%).

st.2: The FSSAI 'Eat Right Place of Worship' certificate of the Ayodhya Ram Temple is valid for life.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the certificate is valid for two years (till October 2028).

st.2: Its '5C' model includes Care.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 5Cs are Connect, Converse, Co-create, Contribute and Continue; Care is not one of them.

st.2: Its original 2024 deadline has been kept unchanged.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the deadline was extended from 2024 to December 2028 as JJM 2.0.
Both statements are correct: the ESIC scheme runs till 30 June 2027 and pays 50% of average daily wage for up to 90 days, once in a lifetime.

st.1: It is a centrally sponsored scheme for Scheduled Tribes.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: PM-AJAY (2021-22) is for Scheduled Castes, run by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

st.1: BIS was the predecessor of the Indian Standards Institution.
st.2: BIS functions as a non-statutory society.
st.4: The headquarters of BIS is in Mumbai.

x: Statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: BIS (1987) succeeded the Indian Standards Institution (1947). Statement 2 is wrong: BIS is a statutory body under the BIS Act, 2016. Statement 4 is wrong: BIS is headquartered at New Delhi.

st.2: WHO guidelines of 2019 encouraged screen exposure for children.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: WHO's 2019 guidelines advised limiting screen time for young children.

st.1: An industrial node at Gaya is planned on the New Delhi–Kolkata Industrial Corridor.

x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Gaya node is on the Amritsar–Kolkata Industrial Corridor.

st.3: Ministers cannot be members of a DRSC.
st.4: The DRSC on Finance is chaired by Shashi Tharoor.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: Ministers are not eligible for DRSC membership. Statement 4 is wrong: Shashi Tharoor chairs the External Affairs committee, not the Finance committee.

st.3: The empowered teams on the West Asia conflict were announced after a review by the NITI Aayog Governing Council.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the PM announced seven empowered teams after a review by the Cabinet Committee on Security (24 March 2026).

st.1: The Uday Kotak Committee (2017) on corporate governance of listed companies was set up by the RBI.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Uday Kotak Committee on corporate governance was set up by SEBI.

st.3: The Inland Waterways Authority of India was set up under the Inland Vessels Act, 2021.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: IWAI was set up in 1986 under the Inland Waterways Authority of India Act, 1985.

st.2: Uttarakhand recorded the most new plant taxa.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Arunachal Pradesh recorded the most new plant taxa.

st.2: Phase I reef units were placed far offshore, beyond India's territorial sea.
st.3: They are funded entirely by the State government, without PMMSY support.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Phase I has 22 reef units within 2.5 km of the shore. Statement 3 is wrong: they are funded under PMMSY in the ratio 60:40 between the Centre and the State.

st.3: The National Green Tribunal is monitoring the case, and tourism on the island was not halted.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: about 4,000 tonnes of dry waste burned, harming corals and fisheries, and the NGT is monitoring the matter without halting tourism.

st.3: It was India's first Asia Cup title in the T20 format.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: India had already won the 2016 Asia Cup in the T20 format; 2025 was its 9th title overall.

st.2: It was formerly known as the Greyhounds.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Greyhounds is AP's separate anti-Naxal force; EAGLE grew out of the State's anti-narcotics task force.

st.3: It is paid only for the first child in a family.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Talliki Vandanam gives ₹15,000 per school-going child, with ₹2,000 deducted for school maintenance.

st.2: The Farm to Home model sells farmers' produce through Rythu Bazaars alone.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Farm to Home is not confined to Rythu Bazaars; it links farmers directly to consumers through several channels.

st.3: AP's C-section rate is 42.11% in government hospitals and 67.76% in private hospitals.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: C-SAFE has UNICEF among its partners, Machilipatnam GH raised normal deliveries from 23% to 34%, and AP's C-section rate is 42.11% (government) and 67.76% (private).

st.4: Large industries are among its beneficiary groups.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the programme targets rural households and farm power, not large industries.

st.3: Vision 2047 has three-tier monitoring through District Vision Units, Mandal Vision Units and Gram Sabhas.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the third tier is the Constituency Development Committees, not Gram Sabhas.

st.3: Per capita income is highest in a Rayalaseema district.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Visakhapatnam has the highest per capita income; no Rayalaseema district reaches the State average of ₹2,94,507.

st.2: Aspirants get free coaching but no stipend.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: aspirants also get a stipend of ₹1,500 a month.

st.2: Its theme is 'One State – One Vision'.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the theme is '10 Principles – One Vision'.

st.1: The 10 new PPP medical colleges from 2027-28 include Adoni and Ongole.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Adoni is in the list, but Ongole is not; the others include Madanapalle, Markapuram and Pulivendula.

st.3: India's Foreign Trade Policy 2023 is valid for five years, till 2028.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: FTP 2023 came into effect on 1 April 2023 and has no fixed end date.

st.2: Listing on the AP MSME Exchange costs about ₹1.5–2.2 crore, against about ₹75 lakh on BSE/NSE.
st.4: SIDBI was established in 1990 with its headquarters at Mumbai.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the figures are reversed – about ₹75 lakh on the AP exchange against ₹1.5–2.2 crore on BSE/NSE. Statement 4 is wrong: SIDBI is headquartered at Lucknow.

st.1: Euphorbia ananthapuramensis, Euphorbia chalamensis and Ceropegia andhrica were reported from the Western Ghats.
st.4: Hero stones are called Nadukal in Kannada and Veeragallu in Tamil.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the three new species were reported from AP's Eastern Ghats. Statement 4 is wrong: the names are reversed – Nadukal in Tamil and Veeragallu in Kannada.

st.2: South Central Railway (est. 1966, HQ Secunderabad) keeps the Secunderabad, Hyderabad and Guntakal divisions.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Guntakal goes to the new South Coast Railway; South Central Railway keeps Secunderabad, Hyderabad and Nanded.

st.2: The Airports Authority of India was allowed to prepare the Terms of Reference for seven water aerodromes.
st.3: Gandikota is among the Phase 2 water aerodrome locations.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: it was AP Airports Development Corporation Ltd (APADCL), not the AAI. Statement 3 is wrong: Gandikota is a Phase 1 location.

st.2: The 540 MW solar project of ReNew Vikram Shakti approved under the ICE Policy–2024 is located at Aspari in Kurnool district.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the ReNew 540 MW solar project is at Gooty and Pamidi in Anantapur; Aspari (Kurnool) has JSW's wind project.

st.3: The awards were presented at the 69th Indian Travel Congress at Visakhapatnam.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 69th Indian Travel Congress was held at Kolkata.

st.2: India has not ratified the World Heritage Convention.
st.3: Cultural sites nominated for World Heritage status are evaluated by the IUCN.

x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Convention was adopted in 1972 and India ratified it in 1977. Statement 3 is wrong: cultural sites are evaluated by ICOMOS; IUCN evaluates natural sites.

st.2: He earned the title 'Andhra Kesari' for facing the police during the Salt Satyagraha of 1930.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Prakasam was called 'Andhra Kesari' for baring his chest to police guns during the Simon Commission protest in Madras (1928).

st.2: Kangundi Bouldering is part of the July 2026 revival plan.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Kangundi Bouldering is an APTA festival, not part of the July 2026 revival plan.

st.3: Awardee Tamogna Mothukuri of Gudivada swam across Lake Geneva at the age of five.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Tamogna Mothukuri swam across Lake Bodensee (6.3 km) at the age of five.
